OPENING IT THE FIRST TIME

Seeing a security warning? That’s expected.

Pixel Buddy is free and open source, and it isn’t signed with a paid Apple or Microsoft certificate yet. So the first time you open it, your computer asks you to confirm. You only do this once.

⌘ macOS

  1. Open Pixel Buddy. When macOS says it “could not verify” the app, click Done.
  2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and scroll down.
  3. Next to the message about Pixel Buddy, click Open Anyway and confirm.
On macOS 14 or earlier, you can Control-click the app and choose Open instead.

⊞ Windows

  1. If you see “Windows protected your PC”, click More info.
  2. Check the app name is pixel-buddy, then click Run anyway.
Your organization’s policies may still block unsigned apps on work computers.

Only do this for files from this site or Pixel Buddy’s GitHub releases, and never turn off Gatekeeper or SmartScreen. Apple’s guide ↗

A FEW LITTLE ANSWERS

Before you say hello.

Is it really free?

Yes. Pixel Buddy is free and open source under the MIT license. You can use it, share it, and make it your own.

What stays on my device?

The app stores your preferences, media, and daily counters locally. The Chrome extension keeps its settings in your browser and never reads or sends the pages you visit. There is no account or analytics service. This website contacts GitHub to check available releases. Read the privacy policy.

What should I know before installing?

Desktop builds aren’t signed with a paid certificate yet, so macOS asks you to allow the app in Privacy & Security and Windows may show SmartScreen the first time. See the one-time steps. Download only from this site or the project’s GitHub releases.

On macOS, optional smart monitoring uses Accessibility permission. You can turn monitoring off and use regular timers instead.

Can I share it with a friend?

Absolutely. Share the website or GitHub release link so they can choose the right version. Found a bug or have an idea? Tell us on GitHub.
